docSummary: Synthetic fixture (Agency X) describing an application-management engagement covering 12 eServices (Portal, Callup, Manning, Deferment, Payslip, Registration, Clearance, Pay, Awards, Leave&Claims, Retail, Posting) plus two separate automation improvement ideas (account-review and log-analysis). The FY25 eServices table explicitly covers April 2025-March 2026 (12 months), so period totals were divided by 12: incidents (Sev A+B+C = 636) ≈ 53/month, SRs (3066) ≈ 255.5/month, CRs (202) ≈ 16.8/month. Severity mapped to P1-P4 as Sev A→P1 (155/636=24.37%), Sev B→P2 (474/636=74.53%), Sev C→P3 (7/636=1.10%), P4=0%. SR complexity stated as 'majority simple' with 10-20% urgent/complex, mapped to low≈85%/high≈15%. L1 is explicitly out of scope (agency's own help desk); an unusual intermediate 'L1.5' team (3-4 people, 24x7) resolves 20-30% of tickets, <5% of the remainder escalates to L3, the rest goes to L2 - used to approximate pass12≈75%/pass23≈5%, though this mapping is imperfect since L1.5 is not a standard tier. Incumbent services team sized 30-36 FTE (midpoint 33 used); an 18-FTE platform team and Singapore-region cloud hosting are run by a separate vendor/tender and excluded from towers. Several figures look anomalous (Callup alone holds 140 of 155 total Sev A; Retail has 890 SRs vs 1 CR; Leave&Claims has 1600 SRs vs 10 CRs; an earlier session's platform-wide Sev A figure of 6 conflicts with the table's 155) and are flagged for verification. A page-5 bid-team AI-generated pod/FTE estimate was excluded as it is not client-stated fact.

warnings: An 'L1.5' team of 3-4 people (24x7, manual ticket filtering/routing) is a special intermediate team, not a standard L1/L2/L3 tier; pass12/pass23 were approximated from its stated percentages and should be checked.
The 18-FTE platform team and the Singapore-region cloud hosting are run by a separate hosting vendor/separate tender - not included as a tower, per instructions.
Conflicting user counts: 'Fewer than 1000 users are supported' (session 2) vs '4000 concurrent users at maximum' (governance, session 2) - verify which applies.
'12 eServices in total; one (Booklet) being decommissioned' (session 3) does not reconcile with the FY25 table which lists 12 active eServices (not 11) - verify actual in-scope count.

Sev A conflict: an earlier session reported platform-wide Sev A = 6 for FY25, but the FY25 table total Sev A is 155 (driven almost entirely by Callup=140, ~90% of the Sev A total) - flagged by the bid team itself as suspect; verify before use.
Retail shows 890 SRs but only 1 CR and 54 job failures, and Leave and Claims shows 1600 SRs but only 10 CRs - both ratios look anomalous and were flagged by the bid team as numbers to challenge.
Job Failures (92 over FY25, ~7.7/month) are reported separately in the source table but have no dedicated field in this schema; they were not added into inc/sr/cr and are omitted.
Incumbent FTE was quoted as a range (30 to 36); the midpoint (33) was used.
pass12/pass23 derivation mixes the L1.5-level stat (20-30%) and the L3-level stat (<5%) because the source did not give a clean L1->L2->L3 breakdown; treat these as approximate.
Account-review and log-analysis items are separate automation efforts (not part of the ongoing managed service) and were placed in opportunities, not towers.
Page 5 contains a bid-team/AI-generated pod and FTE estimate explicitly marked as not client-stated; none of its figures were used in this extraction.
No contract term length was stated anywhere in the notes; eng.term was omitted.
